Focusing on distant star clusters in our Milky Way (and in other galaxies), integrated photometry allows us to characterize star clusters in a precise way using synthetic colours. The combination of already available optical and new UV photometry significantly increases the precision due to the small sensitivity to the shape of the extinction curve. To reach the goals, we will use available population synthesis codes to model different star clusters. We can mainly estimate the total masses, ratios of main sequence stars to giants, ages, and possibly metallicities.
